subject.title: Dashboard shows deployment version drift warning

question: Should ClawHub treat frontend/Convex build-SHA mismatch as an actionable dashboard warning, or should expected frontend-only/backend-only deploy drift be downgraded or suppressed?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally warn on any unequal SHAs, while the deployment workflow supports separate frontend and backend targets; changing this without maintainer intent could either hide real skew or keep noisy expected warnings.

options.title: Keep Strict Same-SHA Warning
options.body: Treat the warning as correct when SHAs differ and fix deployment stamping or release ordering when production drifts.

options.title: Downgrade Expected Partial Drift
options.body: If partial deploys are normal, make the banner copy or severity distinguish expected partial drift from actionable skew and update tests and docs together.

options.title: Disable Drift Detection
options.body: Suppressing the check removes noisy warnings but loses the signal that catches real frontend/backend deployment skew.

recommendation.title: Keep Strict Same-SHA Warning
recommendation.body: Treat the warning as correct when SHAs differ and fix deployment stamping or release ordering when production drifts.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the current drift banner, metadata query, and deployment-stamping implementation in current-main history.
